findings.title: PostHog autocapture element chain leaks the raw data-resume-token past the sanitize_properties scrub
findings.detail: The resume render puts the raw 288-bit continue token on <body data-resume-token> (a read-capability for applicant PII). posthog.init leaves autocapture at the SDK default TRUE (no key in the init config; empirically posthog.config.autocapture===true without it). Verified against posthog-js 1.409.5 source (the version the array loader ships): the autocapture elements-chain builder walks ancestors up to AND INCLUDING <body>, and captures every attribute of non-sensitive elements as attr__<name>. So a consenting applicant's click on the resume page emits an $autocapture event whose $elements_chain contains attr__data-resume-token="<token>". The sanitize_properties regex /(\/(?:resume|draft-erasure)\/)[^\s&#/?]+/g only redacts tokens preceded by a literal /resume/ or /draft-erasure/ path segment — the attribute value is the bare token, no prefix, so it passes through UNREDACTED. The feature's own comment states the invariant: 'the token must never land in the analytics store'.
findings.recommended_fix: Disable autocapture on the apply-form pages (the funnel is custom events) or add element_attribute_ignorelist:['data-resume-token'] to the init; belt-and-braces: extend the scrub to redact attr__data-resume-token values, and strengthen the scrub test (see N12) to assert the replacement, not just the pattern's presence.
findings.verification: confirmed (code read + posthog-js 1.409.5 source-verified chain/attr mechanics + empirical default-true check)

findings.title: Draft-write 413 envelope lacks ok:false — continue-link UI reports 'Link sent' on a rejected request and suppresses the retry
findings.detail: The body-size gate answers 413 {"error":{...}} (no ok key). The continue-link click handler parses the JSON regardless of status, then body.ok === false is false: the UI shows 'Link sent — check your inbox', sets lastSentPayload (suppressing the pagehide beacon), and fires a phantom application_draft_saved — though nothing was saved or emailed. Reachable: form inputs have no maxlength (0 occurrences in form_pages/form_view), ~40 free-text fields can exceed the 64 KB draft-write cap.
findings.recommended_fix: Add ok:false to the 413 JSON envelope (and any other non-handler JSON rejections on these endpoints), or check res.ok in the click handler before parsing.

findings.title: Brand-checked-timers pin never exercises the wrapped clearTimeout seam
findings.detail: The new B1 regression pin fires step-changed exactly once, so trigger() runs with id===null and t.clear is never called; cancel() (pagehide) is also never driven. Reverting `clear` to a detached env.clearTimeout — half of the B1 fix — ships green.
findings.recommended_fix: Fire step-changed twice (trigger's id!==null branch calls t.clear) or dispatch pagehide after a trigger, asserting no throw and correct fetch count.

findings.title: No-oracle doc comment overclaims: ok:false also fires on the upsert-abort arm, not 'only when the Resend call itself failed'
findings.detail: The rewritten docstring states ok:false occurs 'only when the Resend call itself failed', but a failed draft upsert also aborts before the claim with ok:false/200 (draft_handler.gleam:279). The contract text misstates the round-3 response shape.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: ok:false on upsert failure or Resend send failure; ok:true on every claim outcome.

findings.title: Continue-link upsert-failure abort answers 200 ok:false while claim DB failure answers 500 — and save-path upsert failure is also 500
findings.detail: Two server-side DB failures in one handler get different status conventions (200-ok:false vs 500); handle_save_draft's identical upsert failure is 500 (line 219). The client tolerates both, but the inconsistency is undocumented and surprises future callers.
findings.recommended_fix: Pick one convention for DB-failure on these endpoints (500, matching the save path) or document why continue-link deliberately differs.

findings.title: strip_draft_on_submit.sql manually SETs updated_at = now() — dead code the BEFORE UPDATE trigger overwrites, contradicting the migration's stated convention
findings.detail: The migration header states updated_at 'follows the repo's trigger convention ... not manual SETs' and the update_application_draft_updated_at trigger fires on every UPDATE; claim/clear/erase/mark_resumed all rely on it. Strip's manual SET is dead weight contradicting the file's own convention.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the updated_at = now() line from strip_draft_on_submit.sql.

findings.title: saveNow's keepalive fetch throws synchronously for >64 KiB bodies, escaping the promise chain on every step change
findings.detail: Per the Fetch spec a keepalive request whose body exceeds 64 KiB throws a TypeError synchronously (Request construction), before any promise exists — the .catch never runs and the exception propagates uncaught out of the debounce listener. Reachable: inputs have no maxlength; ~40 free-text fields can exceed 64 KiB.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap the fetch call in try/catch (leave state dirty) or cap serialized payload size client-side before send.

findings.title: Spec claims the serializer skips hidden inputs; shouldSkipControl has no hidden-type arm

findings.title: PostHog token-scrub pinned only by substring presence — a regex regression that disables redaction keeps both pinned substrings and stays green
findings.detail: The test asserts only 'sanitize_properties:function(p)' and 'resume|draft-erasure' substrings; the replacement ('$1<redacted>') and character class — the parts that actually redact — are unasserted. (B1's autocapture bypass proves the scrub needs a stronger pin.)
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the replacement string and the negated char class, or drive the scrub function against a tokenised URL in a JS test.
